players.product: The Generate Platform (machine-learning generative biology; computational design integrated with large-scale biological experimentation) and AI-engineered protein therapeutics such as GB-0895

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 SOLAIRIA Phase 3 status and timing (CFO Jason Silvers): the two studies (SOLAIRIA-1 and SOLAIRIA-2) total 786 subjects; Generate opened the study in December 2025 and now has regulatory approval in 39 of the 42 expected countries across 6 different global regions. Generate expects to complete enrollment by the end of 2027; with a 52-week follow-up it expects Phase 3 asthma data by the end of 2028 / early 2029. The primary endpoint is exacerbation reduction; the study is powered at about 94% on the low-EOS population, which powers it at 99% on the entire study; a key inclusion criterion is 2 exacerbations in the 12 months before enrollment.
quarterly_data.figure: regulatory approval in 39 of 42 countries; enrollment complete by end of 2027; Phase 3 asthma data by end of 2028 / early 2029; ~94% power (low EOS), 99% (entire study)

quarterly_data.signal: Platform scale (CEO Michael Nally and CFO Jason Silvers): Generate has now put five molecules into the clinic, and the CEO says the technology is scalable enough to start somewhere between five and 10 programs a year, for its own pipeline and for partners such as Amgen and Novartis. The CFO says Generate measures on the order of billions and has 4 cryo-electron microscopes that view protein-protein interactions dynamically at atomistic resolution, and that while models may commoditize, its differentiated training data will lead to better results. The CEO says Generate has torn up its digital infrastructure three times in eight years and, around the turn of the year, recognised that an agentic approach to science would be the future.
quarterly_data.figure: five molecules in the clinic; capacity to start five to 10 programs a year; 4 cryo-electron microscopes

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 Phase 1-to-Phase 3 rationale (CEO and CFO): following GSK's mepolizumab approach, the Phase 1 enrolled mild-to-moderate asthmatics and showed biomarker modulation to the same degree as Tezspire; modelling showed 99.9% target occupancy over the entire six-month course; Tezspire's Phase 2 saw no difference in exacerbations across an eightfold exposure range, so the CEO says Generate chose not to 'spend $50 million and wait two years for a phase II readout'. CFO: GB-0895 hits the same epitope as tezepelumab; across 6 doses from 10 to 1,200 milligrams suppression did not improve above 300 milligrams, and in COPD there was no difference between 300 and 600 milligrams, so 'we feel really confident 300 milligrams is the right dose.'
quarterly_data.figure: 99.9% target occupancy over six months; skipped a Phase 2 of ~$50 million and two years; 300 milligram dose

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 competition and market (CEO views): having started Phase 3 in December, Generate believes it is at least 9 to 12 months ahead of the other long-acting anti-TSLP antibodies, and says order of entry has historically driven market share in such classes. On Sanofi's IL-13/TSLP bispecific data the CEO saw no real difference versus monotherapy in exacerbations or lung function, easing the perceived threat of combination therapy; Generate saw a 50% reduction in IL-13 in its TSLP studies. Biologic penetration in asthma is about 20% versus 40%-60% in mature immunology indications, and only about 20% of severe asthma patients are maximally adherent; the CEO expects six-monthly dosing to yield real-world efficacy and hospital-utilisation benefits.
quarterly_data.figure: at least 9 to 12 months ahead of other long-acting anti-TSLPs; asthma biologic penetration about 20%

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 in COPD next steps (CFO, CEO): the Phase 1b used an EOS cutoff of 200; Generate has had regulatory interactions that are continuing and believes there is a path, similar to asthma, into later-stage COPD trials, a decision it will evaluate over the next several weeks or months alongside its cash position (just under $460 million as of June 30), its oncology trials and the competitive landscape. CEO view: biologic therapy is about 1%-2% penetrated in COPD across most of Europe, and about 28% of the population has eosinophils above 300, where Dupixent and Nucala are indicated; a broader label would help formulary positioning.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase 1b EOS cutoff 200; COPD later-stage decision over the next several weeks or months

quarterly_data.signal: GB-4362 (MMAE neutralizer) Phase 1 plan (CFO, CEO): the Phase 1 runs at multiple leading cancer centers including MD Anderson, City of Hope and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; the dose-escalation part seeks the dose that reduces free MMAE by 50% (preclinically up to 80% reduction cut cytotoxicities without impacting tumor killing), which Generate expects over the next several months or early in 2027. It then plans an expansion cohort of about 40 patients with grade 1 peripheral neuropathy on PADCEV and KEYTRUDA, with proof-of-concept data expected in 2027. CEO: the program could be approved faster than the TSLP program, with a registrational path of probably about 200 patients.
quarterly_data.figure: target 50% free-MMAE reduction; dose by early 2027; expansion cohort about 40 patients; proof-of-concept data in 2027; registrational path ~200 patients
